deepdive.sec: Affordable Housing Finance (NBFC-HFC) — small-ticket self-construction / self-purchase home loans + LAP to self-employed, tier-3/tier-4 India

bull_bear.body: Net worth **Rs. 3,198 crores**; leverage **3x**; capital adequacy ~55% (analyst-stated, uncontested). Explicit sequencing: grow into the balance sheet to **4x-4.5x leverage** first, and only then consider *"whether to raise the funds, QIP or something"*. No dividend or buyback commentary on this call. Off-book channels (DA at 15%-16%, co-lending ~4%-5%) are used to manage the **PBC ratio at 64% vs a 60% regulatory threshold**, not to release capital. Provisioning policy is deliberately over-capitalised relative to rules: **Rs. 87 crores ECL vs Rs. 47 crores** required — *"we have created a briefly 2x buffer of what the regulatory threshold. And we have always kept that kind of threshold historically."*
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **The growth guidance was cut, and the cut is management-chosen.** 30%-35% → 25%-30%; login-to-sanction throttled to 45%-47% via the BRE. If the "cautionary environment" persists, FY27 disbursement growth of "beyond 20%" is the floor that has to hold for the 27%-28% AUM CAGR to work.
- **The AUM-vs-disbursement growth gap is unresolved.** Two analysts (Mayank Mistry, Satyam Kumar) pressed on how ~20% disbursement growth produces ~27% AUM growth; the answer was **only** falling BT-out — *"anything above 20% on that piece is going to stretch to the positivity"* — with no quantified runoff bridge. If BT-out stops falling (and management concedes the current low is partly a cautious-cycle artefact), the AUM guidance breaks.
- **Margin quality:** the 9.5% print embeds non-recurring Q4 NPA-resolution interest; disbursement yield (14.6%) is already below portfolio yield (14.8%).
- **Macro on the borrower base:** Middle East war → **LPG / commercial gas supply disruption**, uneven and abnormal monsoon hitting agricultural cash flows and informal income. MD: *"instantly we don't feel that there is any impact in terms of their behavior particularly, but still we feel it's a watchful situation… Things look okay till the month of March."* **The call explicitly defers the read to the following quarter** — *"This quarter is going to play, give output in terms of that piece."*
- **Asset-quality improvement is mechanical, not fresh-flow.** GS3 1.2% came from SARFAESI resolution of the Q2 bulge on a 6-8 month lag; the Stage-2 overlay suggests management itself is not calling an all-clear.
- **Regulatory:** RBI's ECL circular sets minimum 1.5% (home loan) / 2.5% (LAP) thresholds — CFO says *"they are not applicable to us"*, but the company pre-emptively buffered to Stage-2 anyway. **CLM-1 co-lending remains blocked with no timeline.**
- **Two internally inconsistent disclosures on this one call** — co-lending 4% (MD) vs 5% (CFO) of book, and two different fixed/floating asset splits. Minor individually, but both concern the same LAP/rate-risk area.
- **Concentration:** Rajasthan still 30%+ of AUM; the de-concentration path is a five-year one.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body:
Confident and specific on operating metrics (login ratios, branch math, rate-reset buckets) and notably willing to disclose a **self-imposed slowdown** rather than dress it as demand weakness — the BRE-tightening admission and the login-ratio disclosure are the kind of numbers most lenders bury. The CFO volunteered the NPA-resolution distortion in the NIM **without being asked**, which is a genuine credibility marker. Tone is candid on macro uncertainty (*"we have to keep our fingers crossed"*; *"instantly today we don't have answer for that piece"*) rather than promotional.

Against that: the guidance downgrade from 30%-35% to 25%-30% was **not surfaced in the opening remarks** — it took Kunal Shah's question to name it as a change. The MD deflected a direct question on whether Q4 was the disbursement-growth bottom (*"Please don't allow me to compare between Q4 and how the Q1 has to work on"*), and the competition answer was pure assertion (*"it is not a point of concern at all"*) with no data. English is loose throughout ("plundered by all kinds of competition", "that isn't titled up purposely"), so several answers require careful reading. Two numeric self-contradictions in one call (§10) is a small but real disclosure-discipline flag.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **The binding constraint is the credit engine, not demand.** Logins are rising while sanctions are being cut — the guidance downgrade is a *supply* decision management can reverse quickly (*"as the time came back in a conducive form, I think we should be able to pick up quickly"*). Login-to-sanction is therefore the single leading indicator to track: 45%-47% now vs a 55%-58% normal. That makes this a **throttle, not a brake** — a distinction most affordable-HFC slowdowns don't offer.
- **The AUM guidance is load-bearing on BT-out, which is cyclically flattered.** Management admits low BT-out is partly an artefact of a cautious market (*"you always find for everyone BT-out is always normally on a lower side"*). Growth guided at 27%-28% AUM off 20% disbursements only works while runoff stays suppressed — so an *improving* macro would paradoxically pressure the AUM bridge even as it lifts disbursements.
- **DA and co-lending are PBC instruments, not strategy.** Both exist to shift LAP off-book and hold PBC at 64% vs the 60% floor. Read the "softness in DA drawdown" and the co-lending stall as regulatory-ratio management, not a change in business model — and note the company is content to abandon co-lending entirely (*"it is not something which we have to worry around at all"*), unusual among peers building it as a growth channel.
- **Rate-cycle asymmetry is now deliberately engineered.** Only ~7%-8% of the fixed-rate book is funded by variable-rate liabilities (from ~33% two years ago, heading to ~5%). India Shelter has been converting a falling-rate windfall into structural rate-risk removal rather than into growth — consistent with the "return ratios rather than growth alone" framing in the opening remarks.
- **The 9.5% margin should not be extrapolated.** Q4 NPA-resolution interest recovery is in it, and disbursement yield already prints below portfolio yield. The >6% *spread* commitment, not the margin level, is the number management has actually bound itself to.
- **Silent on the reduction in ROE headroom from over-provisioning:** ECL at 2x the regulatory requirement plus a 2% Stage-2 overlay is a conservative posture that management says it will *not* extend further — meaning FY27 credit cost of 40-50 bps has no further buffer-build inside it, which is mildly favourable for FY27 PAT.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Capital is held well above requirement - CRAR 59.1% and leverage of 3.0x at Q1FY27 - with book value per share of Rs. 308.0; CRAR has trended down from 109% in FY17 as the balance sheet levered up modestly.
- Liability franchise is deliberately diversified: 32 lender relationships, average tenure of borrowings of 8 years, and a Q1FY27 funding mix of Term Loans by Banks & FI 42%, DA 22%, NHB 16%, Co-Lending 6%, SIDBI 5%, PTC 4%, ECB 3%, NCD 2%.
- Liquidity is run with a surplus: total liquidity of Rs. 2,423 Cr as of June-26 (cash and equivalents plus Rs. 1,565 Cr of un-availed sanctions from banks/FI), and the deck projects closing liquidity rising to Rs. 2,736 Cr by Q1FY28 "without including any fresh disbursement and borrowing".
- Ratings have been upgraded steadily from BB+ (Stable) in 2012 through A- (Stable) 2016, A (Stable) 2019, A+ (Stable) 2022, A+ (Positive) 2023 to AA- (Stable) in 2024 (CARE Rating, ICRA & IND RA).
- Employee alignment via a 9% ESOP pool covering 726 employees, described as ~40% of employees excluding frontline staff; the deck makes no mention of dividends or buybacks.

business.body:
Standalone HFC, no subsidiaries discussed.
- **Home Loans:** 56%-57% of disbursement; **~56% of AUM**. Focus is **self-construction and self-purchase** in tier-3/tier-4 markets, deliberately *not* builder-tied: *"We don't have a tie up with the builders in terms of that affordable segment builder or something… we are not available to those large markets of tier 1 or tier 2 with a tie-up of the builder particularly."* HL share drifted up in Q2/Q3 FY26 to serve PBC.
- **LAP:** the balance of disbursement; **~98% backed by SORP (self-occupied residential property)** — *"and this is improving as we progress in time."*
- **Direct Assignment (DA):** run as a PBC-management tool, not a growth lever — *"For us, DA is majorly for our PBC requirements… we want to be in the range of 15% to 18% of DA and we are maintaining that 15%-16%."* Softness in Q4 DA drawdown was intentional.
- **Co-lending:** book **Rs. 450-460 crores**, described by MD as *"around approximately 4% of business"* (CFO separately said *"about 5% of the book in form of co-lending, which is primarily pertained to LAP only"* — **the two figures were given on the same call and are not reconciled**). Model used is **CLM-2**; CLM-1 blocked on regulation — *"For CLM1, I think we have to wait some more time. If you ask me exact timeline, it will be difficult at this juncture."* Both DA and co-lending exist chiefly to move LAP off-book and protect PBC at 64% vs the 60% threshold.
- **Geographic mix:** Rajasthan is the flagship at **30%+ of AUM**, guided down to *"maybe 25%-26%"* over five years as South (AP/Telangana/Tamil Nadu), UP and Gujarat scale — framed as a deliberate diversification hedge: *"if Karnataka is a disruption in South, then definitely AP, Telangana and Tamil Nadu is going to support."*

business.body:
- **Diversification-as-underwriting-moat, evidenced by scale:** *"our distribution is spread across 15 states. At this scale, at this level, very few companies have experimented to go into those markets at all. With time, the maturity is coming, that prudency is coming in terms of underwriting, as we keep creating our own vintage in these kind of states."*
- **Collateral quality:** **~98% of the LAP book is SORP** — an unusually hard collateral base for a LAP-heavy affordable lender, and the reason SARFAESI resolution works organically.
- **Retention machine lowering BT-out:** BT-out down to **4.5%, −80 bps YoY, "lowest among last 3-4 years"**, attributed to a customer-engagement unit set up ~a year ago plus a customer app *"which have now almost all the customers which is on our board"*. Management is candid that part of this is cyclical, not structural: *"In particular time when situation is always alarming and cautionary… you always find for everyone BT-out is always normally on a lower side basically."*
- **Fixed-rate book as a BT-out shield:** ~48% of AUM is pure fixed-rate, +37% semi-variable (fixed for the first three years) — CFO: *"that is again one of the good sectors which support us in terms of BT-out."*
- **Barrier framing on competition:** *"any new player which is entering, they have their own hurdles around that piece to venture that market… It is only your ability to execute in those markets that matters."*

- "India Shelter provides affordable home loans and loan against property in Tier 2 and 3 geographies in India for last 16 years", focused on "customers from low-and middle-income segments who are building or buying their first homes".

latest_quarter.body:
Yield held with a **10 bps YoY decline in portfolio yield to 14.8%** while Q4 disbursement yield printed **14.6%** — i.e. new business is being written a touch below the back book. On the liability side, **bucket cost of funds 8.2%** and **Q4 marginal cost of funds 7.9%**, so incremental spreads are the wider ones; management explicitly credits the rate cycle: *"this has been a great year in terms of your cost of borrowing, because of market slashing down in terms of cost, and we get a benefit on that piece."* Cost of borrowing was down "about 10 to 15 basis points" in the quarter — which the analyst correctly noted does **not** explain the full 9.1% → 9.5% margin move; the CFO closed the gap with the **NPA-resolution interest recovery** (see §2 one-offs).

**Funding structure:** >30 counterparties, **NHB share stable at 15%**, **average borrowing tenure >8 years**. Q4 saw a **Rs. 378 crore NHB drawdown at 7.5%** with *"a balance of more than Rs. 300 crores for drawdown in Q1."*

**Asset-liability rate mix (CFO's reiterated, authoritative version at the end of the call):** ~**15%** of AUM variable-rate · ~**37%** semi-variable (fixed for three years then variable) · ~**48%** pure fixed. Of that 48% fixed book: ~25% funded by equity, ~17% by fixed-rate borrowings, and the residual **7%-8%** is fixed-rate assets funded by variable-rate liabilities — down from ~33% in Mar-24, targeted to ~5% in FY27. ⚠️ Earlier in the same Q&A the CFO gave a materially different cut (*"around 13%-14% of book which is on floating… that book is again now around 10%-12%, which means approximately 70%, 65%-70% book that continue to remain on the fixed"*), which prompted Kunal Shah's clarification request. Both are recorded; the 15/37/48 reiteration is the one management chose to restate.

**Cost line:** OPEX +26% YoY against AUM +29% → OPEX/AUM **3.94%**, −20 bps, and cost-to-income **36%**, ~−100 bps, for both quarter and year.

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q4 FY26 (this):** AUM Rs. 11,044 cr (+29% YoY, +7% QoQ); first Rs. 1,000 cr+ disbursement quarter; PAT Rs. 138 cr (+27% YoY, +11% QoQ); FY26 PAT crossed Rs. 500 cr; ROE 17.6%; net worth Rs. 3,198 cr; leverage 3x. Portfolio yield 14.8% (−10 bps), Q4 disb yield 14.6%, bucket CoF 8.2% / marginal 7.9%; reported margin 9.1%→9.5% (part NPA-resolution interest). GS3 1.2% (−29/30 bps QoQ), NS3 0.9%, 30+ 4% (−100 bps); credit cost 30 bps Q / 50 bps FY incl. Rs. 5 cr Stage-2 overlay; ECL Rs. 87 cr vs Rs. 47 cr regulatory. OPEX/AUM 3.94% (−20 bps), C/I 36% (−100 bps). BT-out 4.5% (−80 bps). 307 branches (+41 FY), 15 states, 4,800 staff. PBC 64%. **Guidance CUT: medium-term loan growth 30-35% → 25-30%; FY27 disbursement growth "beyond 20%"; spread >6%; credit cost 40-50 bps; 40-45 branches/yr; Rs. 30,000 cr AUM by 2030; no capital raise until ~4.5x leverage.**
- _Q1 FY27 → check: **did login-to-sanction recover toward 55%?** (the reversibility test); disbursement growth actually printing >20%; whether the LPG/monsoon stress showed up in 30+ DPD as mgmt deferred it to "this quarter"; NHB Rs. 300 cr+ Q1 drawdown taken; margin ex-NPA-recovery (is 9.5% held or does it fall back toward 9.1%?); BT-out — does 4.5% hold or revert as macro normalises; Stage-2 overlay left untouched as promised; fixed-book-funded-by-variable progress toward 5%; co-lending / CLM-1 still zero; ATS still ~Rs. 10 lakh._

outlook.body:
Stated verbatim in the opening remarks as "the guidance for the coming times":
- **Loan growth 25% to 30% for the next 3 years**, with "a clear goal of reaching **Rs. 30,000 crores AUM by 2030**". ⚠️ **This is a cut** — Kunal Shah: *"earlier we indicated 30%-35% maybe over the medium term. Now, we are suggesting that it will be 25% to 30%."* MD's arithmetic: *"even if we maintain this 27%-28% of growth for next 3-4 years, we will be able to achieve that Rs. 30,000 crores."*
- **Spread: "Maintaining the spreads of more than 6% in the medium term."** Restated: *"our first priority on the field… is always to maintain the spread, which is beyond 6%."*
- **Credit cost: 40 to 50 bps.** (FY26 actual 50 bps.) CFO confirmed the overlay buffer is already built and *"at this point of time, we don't have any plans to further stack up the buffers."*
- **Branch addition ~40 to 45 per year** (307 today → *"going to reach by 2030 up to 500 branches"*).
- **FY27 disbursement growth: "beyond 20%"** — *"this year we will cross 20% of disbursement number which we are quite confident of and we will do anyway beyond that piece. We will be easily achieving 27%-28% of AUM growth."* Explicitly a first-year floor: *"That is for the first year particularly. This can't be sustainable for long term. We have to definitely pull it up."*
- **OPEX-to-AUM: down 15-20 bps every year** — *"Every year, it should come down by 15 to 20 bps and things look very well on track."*
- **Fixed-rate book funded by variable-rate liabilities: down to ~5% in FY27** (from ~33% in Mar-24 to ~8% now).
- **HL:LAP disbursement mix held** at 56%-57% HL / rest LAP — *"there should not be much of difference between LAP and HL in Financial Year '27 also. That is going to remain the same ratio."*
- **DA share held at 15%-16%** of a targeted 15%-18% band.
- **Co-lending: explicitly zero in the plan** — *"In our plan, in our budget, we are not including any of the numbers which is around the co-lending."*
- **Capital: no raise until leverage ~4.5x** — *"today leverage is 3x. I think we would like to go to the level of leverage around 4x and 4.5x times… as we reach around 4.5x in terms of leverage, we will be then thinking about how to take it to the next level, whether to raise the funds, QIP or something."*
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)

outlook.body: Not an order-book business; the pipeline proxy is **login → sanction conversion**, and it is the single most important disclosure on this call. MD: *"if you talk about log-in to sanction ratio, during normal days, it used to be around 55%-58%… Today, that is less than 50%. It had even bottomed down to the level of 40% to 43%… that 43%-45%, which has in month of this quarter, particularly has slightly inched up to 45%-47%. But in normal circumstances, it should be around 55%."* Crucially the constraint is **self-imposed, not demand-side**: *"our logins are increasing day by day. But our business rule engine, the credit engine that has to function that isn't titled up purposely keeping mind all the aspects which is happening there. So, we have been a little cautious in that way."* Distribution base: **307 branches, 15 states, 4,800 employees**; digital channel now disbursing **Rs. 20-30 crores** (vs "single digit" a year to eighteen months ago).

outlook.body:
- **Branch expansion at a falling marginal cost:** *"earlier the 40-45 branches, we were opening on a smaller base. Now, on the base of 307 branches which we exist today, the 45 is hardly 13%-14% which used to be, say, 18%-20% a few years back"* → 500 branches by 2030.
- **Productivity drive** — "per case, per employee, number of cases that has to keep improving" in the *same* geographies.
- **Digital origination:** from single-digit crores to **Rs. 20-30 crores** of disbursement, started ~a year ago.
- **Ticket-size creep:** growth in the 15-25 lakh and 25 lakh+ buckets is real but off "almost negligible base" and only "handful of cases"; ATS ~Rs. 10 lakh, guided to *"maybe 10.5 in, say, 2, 3, 4 quarters beyond"* — explicitly **not** an immediate lever.
- **Balance-sheet headroom:** leverage 3x against an analyst-cited ~55% capital adequacy, unused until 4.5x.

deepdive.thesis: A clean FY26 finish — AUM Rs. 11,044 crores (+29% YoY), first-ever Rs. 1,000 crore+ disbursement quarter, PAT Rs. 138 crores (+27% YoY), ROE 17.6%, and Gross Stage-3 down to 1.2% as SARFAESI resolutions from the Q2 NPA bulge came through organically. The real news is a **deliberate step-down in the growth ambition**: medium-term guidance cut from the earlier 30%-35% to **25%-30% loan growth**, with FY27 disbursement growth guided only "beyond 20%", because management has purposely tightened the business rule engine — login-to-sanction has fallen from a normal 55%-58% to 45%-47% (having bottomed at 40%-43%). Management frames this as temporary caution in a "cautionary environment" (Middle East war, LPG shortage, uneven monsoon), not a demand problem, and holds the Rs. 30,000 crore-by-2030 AUM goal on 27%-28% CAGR. Spread discipline (>6%) and a 2x-regulatory ECL buffer are the trade-off for the slower top line.

risks & watch-items:
- **The growth guidance was cut, and the cut is management-chosen.** 30%-35% → 25%-30%; login-to-sanction throttled to 45%-47% via the BRE. If the "cautionary environment" persists, FY27 disbursement growth of "beyond 20%" is the floor that has to hold for the 27%-28% AUM CAGR to work.
- **The AUM-vs-disbursement growth gap is unresolved.** Two analysts (Mayank Mistry, Satyam Kumar) pressed on how ~20% disbursement growth produces ~27% AUM growth; the answer was **only** falling BT-out — *"anything above 20% on that piece is going to stretch to the positivity"* — with no quantified runoff bridge. If BT-out stops falling (and management concedes the current low is partly a cautious-cycle artefact), the AUM guidance breaks.
- **Margin quality:** the 9.5% print embeds non-recurring Q4 NPA-resolution interest; disbursement yield (14.6%) is already below portfolio yield (14.8%).
- **Macro on the borrower base:** Middle East war → **LPG / commercial gas supply disruption**, uneven and abnormal monsoon hitting agricultural cash flows and informal income. MD: *"instantly we don't feel that there is any impact in terms of their behavior particularly, but still we feel it's a watchful situation… Things look okay till the month of March."* **The call explicitly defers the read to the following quarter** — *"This quarter is going to play, give output in terms of that piece."*
- **Asset-quality improvement is mechanical, not fresh-flow.** GS3 1.2% came from SARFAESI resolution of the Q2 bulge on a 6-8 month lag; the Stage-2 overlay suggests management itself is not calling an all-clear.
- **Regulatory:** RBI's ECL circular sets minimum 1.5% (home loan) / 2.5% (LAP) thresholds — CFO says *"they are not applicable to us"*, but the company pre-emptively buffered to Stage-2 anyway. **CLM-1 co-lending remains blocked with no timeline.**
- **Two internally inconsistent disclosures on this one call** — co-lending 4% (MD) vs 5% (CFO) of book, and two different fixed/floating asset splits. Minor individually, but both concern the same LAP/rate-risk area.
- **Concentration:** Rajasthan still 30%+ of AUM; the de-concentration path is a five-year one.
management quality / tone:
Confident and specific on operating metrics (login ratios, branch math, rate-reset buckets) and notably willing to disclose a **self-imposed slowdown** rather than dress it as demand weakness — the BRE-tightening admission and the login-ratio disclosure are the kind of numbers most lenders bury. The CFO volunteered the NPA-resolution distortion in the NIM **without being asked**, which is a genuine credibility marker. Tone is candid on macro uncertainty (*"we have to keep our fingers crossed"*; *"instantly today we don't have answer for that piece"*) rather than promotional.

Against that: the guidance downgrade from 30%-35% to 25%-30% was **not surfaced in the opening remarks** — it took Kunal Shah's question to name it as a change. The MD deflected a direct question on whether Q4 was the disbursement-growth bottom (*"Please don't allow me to compare between Q4 and how the Q1 has to work on"*), and the competition answer was pure assertion (*"it is not a point of concern at all"*) with no data. English is loose throughout ("plundered by all kinds of competition", "that isn't titled up purposely"), so several answers require careful reading. Two numeric self-contradictions in one call (§10) is a small but real disclosure-discipline flag.
non-obvious takeaways:
- **The binding constraint is the credit engine, not demand.** Logins are rising while sanctions are being cut — the guidance downgrade is a *supply* decision management can reverse quickly (*"as the time came back in a conducive form, I think we should be able to pick up quickly"*). Login-to-sanction is therefore the single leading indicator to track: 45%-47% now vs a 55%-58% normal. That makes this a **throttle, not a brake** — a distinction most affordable-HFC slowdowns don't offer.
- **The AUM guidance is load-bearing on BT-out, which is cyclically flattered.** Management admits low BT-out is partly an artefact of a cautious market (*"you always find for everyone BT-out is always normally on a lower side"*). Growth guided at 27%-28% AUM off 20% disbursements only works while runoff stays suppressed — so an *improving* macro would paradoxically pressure the AUM bridge even as it lifts disbursements.
- **DA and co-lending are PBC instruments, not strategy.** Both exist to shift LAP off-book and hold PBC at 64% vs the 60% floor. Read the "softness in DA drawdown" and the co-lending stall as regulatory-ratio management, not a change in business model — and note the company is content to abandon co-lending entirely (*"it is not something which we have to worry around at all"*), unusual among peers building it as a growth channel.
- **Rate-cycle asymmetry is now deliberately engineered.** Only ~7%-8% of the fixed-rate book is funded by variable-rate liabilities (from ~33% two years ago, heading to ~5%). India Shelter has been converting a falling-rate windfall into structural rate-risk removal rather than into growth — consistent with the "return ratios rather than growth alone" framing in the opening remarks.
- **The 9.5% margin should not be extrapolated.** Q4 NPA-resolution interest recovery is in it, and disbursement yield already prints below portfolio yield. The >6% *spread* commitment, not the margin level, is the number management has actually bound itself to.
- **Silent on the reduction in ROE headroom from over-provisioning:** ECL at 2x the regulatory requirement plus a 2% Stage-2 overlay is a conservative posture that management says it will *not* extend further — meaning FY27 credit cost of 40-50 bps has no further buffer-build inside it, which is mildly favourable for FY27 PAT.

- **FY27 disbursement growth: "beyond 20%"** — *"this year we will cross 20% of disbursement number which we are quite confident of and we will do anyway beyond that piece. We will be easily achieving 27%-28% of AUM growth."* Explicitly a first-year floor: *"That is for the first year particularly. This can't be sustainable for long term. We have to definitely pull it up."*
- **OPEX-to-AUM: down 15-20 bps every year** — *"Every year, it should come down by 15 to 20 bps and things look very well on track."*
- **Fixed-rate book funded by variable-rate liabilities: down to ~5% in FY27** (from ~33% in Mar-24 to ~8% now).
- **HL:LAP disbursement mix held** at 56%-57% HL / rest LAP — *"there should not be much of difference between LAP and HL in Financial Year '27 also. That is going to remain the same ratio."*
- **DA share held at 15%-16%** of a targeted 15%-18% band.
- **Co-lending: explicitly zero in the plan** — *"In our plan, in our budget, we are not including any of the numbers which is around the co-lending."*
- **Capital: no raise until leverage ~4.5x** — *"today leverage is 3x. I think we would like to go to the level of leverage around 4x and 4.5x times… as we reach around 4.5x in terms of leverage, we will be then thinking about how to take it to the next level, whether to raise the funds, QIP or something."*

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **Branch expansion at a falling marginal cost:** *"earlier the 40-45 branches, we were opening on a smaller base. Now, on the base of 307 branches which we exist today, the 45 is hardly 13%-14% which used to be, say, 18%-20% a few years back"* → 500 branches by 2030.
- **Productivity drive** — "per case, per employee, number of cases that has to keep improving" in the *same* geographies.
- **Digital origination:** from single-digit crores to **Rs. 20-30 crores** of disbursement, started ~a year ago.
- **Ticket-size creep:** growth in the 15-25 lakh and 25 lakh+ buckets is real but off "almost negligible base" and only "handful of cases"; ATS ~Rs. 10 lakh, guided to *"maybe 10.5 in, say, 2, 3, 4 quarters beyond"* — explicitly **not** an immediate lever.
- **Balance-sheet headroom:** leverage 3x against an analyst-cited ~55% capital adequacy, unused until 4.5x.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body:
Yield held with a **10 bps YoY decline in portfolio yield to 14.8%** while Q4 disbursement yield printed **14.6%** — i.e. new business is being written a touch below the back book. On the liability side, **bucket cost of funds 8.2%** and **Q4 marginal cost of funds 7.9%**, so incremental spreads are the wider ones; management explicitly credits the rate cycle: *"this has been a great year in terms of your cost of borrowing, because of market slashing down in terms of cost, and we get a benefit on that piece."* Cost of borrowing was down "about 10 to 15 basis points" in the quarter — which the analyst correctly noted does **not** explain the full 9.1% → 9.5% margin move; the CFO closed the gap with the **NPA-resolution interest recovery** (see §2 one-offs).

**Funding structure:** >30 counterparties, **NHB share stable at 15%**, **average borrowing tenure >8 years**. Q4 saw a **Rs. 378 crore NHB drawdown at 7.5%** with *"a balance of more than Rs. 300 crores for drawdown in Q1."*

**Asset-liability rate mix (CFO's reiterated, authoritative version at the end of the call):** ~**15%** of AUM variable-rate · ~**37%** semi-variable (fixed for three years then variable) · ~**48%** pure fixed. Of that 48% fixed book: ~25% funded by equity, ~17% by fixed-rate borrowings, and the residual **7%-8%** is fixed-rate assets funded by variable-rate liabilities — down from ~33% in Mar-24, targeted to ~5% in FY27. ⚠️ Earlier in the same Q&A the CFO gave a materially different cut (*"around 13%-14% of book which is on floating… that book is again now around 10%-12%, which means approximately 70%, 65%-70% book that continue to remain on the fixed"*), which prompted Kunal Shah's clarification request. Both are recorded; the 15/37/48 reiteration is the one management chose to restate.

**Cost line:** OPEX +26% YoY against AUM +29% → OPEX/AUM **3.94%**, −20 bps, and cost-to-income **36%**, ~−100 bps, for both quarter and year.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Net worth **Rs. 3,198 crores**; leverage **3x**; capital adequacy ~55% (analyst-stated, uncontested). Explicit sequencing: grow into the balance sheet to **4x-4.5x leverage** first, and only then consider *"whether to raise the funds, QIP or something"*. No dividend or buyback commentary on this call. Off-book channels (DA at 15%-16%, co-lending ~4%-5%) are used to manage the **PBC ratio at 64% vs a 60% regulatory threshold**, not to release capital. Provisioning policy is deliberately over-capitalised relative to rules: **Rs. 87 crores ECL vs Rs. 47 crores** required — *"we have created a briefly 2x buffer of what the regulatory threshold. And we have always kept that kind of threshold historically."*

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body:
Confident and specific on operating metrics (login ratios, branch math, rate-reset buckets) and notably willing to disclose a **self-imposed slowdown** rather than dress it as demand weakness — the BRE-tightening admission and the login-ratio disclosure are the kind of numbers most lenders bury. The CFO volunteered the NPA-resolution distortion in the NIM **without being asked**, which is a genuine credibility marker. Tone is candid on macro uncertainty (*"we have to keep our fingers crossed"*; *"instantly today we don't have answer for that piece"*) rather than promotional.

Against that: the guidance downgrade from 30%-35% to 25%-30% was **not surfaced in the opening remarks** — it took Kunal Shah's question to name it as a change. The MD deflected a direct question on whether Q4 was the disbursement-growth bottom (*"Please don't allow me to compare between Q4 and how the Q1 has to work on"*), and the competition answer was pure assertion (*"it is not a point of concern at all"*) with no data. English is loose throughout ("plundered by all kinds of competition", "that isn't titled up purposely"), so several answers require careful reading. Two numeric self-contradictions in one call (§10) is a small but real disclosure-discipline flag.

moat.title: 6a. Moat & competitive position
moat.body:
- **Diversification-as-underwriting-moat, evidenced by scale:** *"our distribution is spread across 15 states. At this scale, at this level, very few companies have experimented to go into those markets at all. With time, the maturity is coming, that prudency is coming in terms of underwriting, as we keep creating our own vintage in these kind of states."*
- **Collateral quality:** **~98% of the LAP book is SORP** — an unusually hard collateral base for a LAP-heavy affordable lender, and the reason SARFAESI resolution works organically.
- **Retention machine lowering BT-out:** BT-out down to **4.5%, −80 bps YoY, "lowest among last 3-4 years"**, attributed to a customer-engagement unit set up ~a year ago plus a customer app *"which have now almost all the customers which is on our board"*. Management is candid that part of this is cyclical, not structural: *"In particular time when situation is always alarming and cautionary… you always find for everyone BT-out is always normally on a lower side basically."*
- **Fixed-rate book as a BT-out shield:** ~48% of AUM is pure fixed-rate, +37% semi-variable (fixed for the first three years) — CFO: *"that is again one of the good sectors which support us in terms of BT-out."*
- **Barrier framing on competition:** *"any new player which is entering, they have their own hurdles around that piece to venture that market… It is only your ability to execute in those markets that matters."*

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
- **The growth guidance was cut, and the cut is management-chosen.** 30%-35% → 25%-30%; login-to-sanction throttled to 45%-47% via the BRE. If the "cautionary environment" persists, FY27 disbursement growth of "beyond 20%" is the floor that has to hold for the 27%-28% AUM CAGR to work.
- **The AUM-vs-disbursement growth gap is unresolved.** Two analysts (Mayank Mistry, Satyam Kumar) pressed on how ~20% disbursement growth produces ~27% AUM growth; the answer was **only** falling BT-out — *"anything above 20% on that piece is going to stretch to the positivity"* — with no quantified runoff bridge. If BT-out stops falling (and management concedes the current low is partly a cautious-cycle artefact), the AUM guidance breaks.
- **Margin quality:** the 9.5% print embeds non-recurring Q4 NPA-resolution interest; disbursement yield (14.6%) is already below portfolio yield (14.8%).
- **Macro on the borrower base:** Middle East war → **LPG / commercial gas supply disruption**, uneven and abnormal monsoon hitting agricultural cash flows and informal income. MD: *"instantly we don't feel that there is any impact in terms of their behavior particularly, but still we feel it's a watchful situation… Things look okay till the month of March."* **The call explicitly defers the read to the following quarter** — *"This quarter is going to play, give output in terms of that piece."*
- **Asset-quality improvement is mechanical, not fresh-flow.** GS3 1.2% came from SARFAESI resolution of the Q2 bulge on a 6-8 month lag; the Stage-2 overlay suggests management itself is not calling an all-clear.
- **Regulatory:** RBI's ECL circular sets minimum 1.5% (home loan) / 2.5% (LAP) thresholds — CFO says *"they are not applicable to us"*, but the company pre-emptively buffered to Stage-2 anyway. **CLM-1 co-lending remains blocked with no timeline.**
- **Two internally inconsistent disclosures on this one call** — co-lending 4% (MD) vs 5% (CFO) of book, and two different fixed/floating asset splits. Minor individually, but both concern the same LAP/rate-risk area.
- **Concentration:** Rajasthan still 30%+ of AUM; the de-concentration path is a five-year one.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- **The binding constraint is the credit engine, not demand.** Logins are rising while sanctions are being cut — the guidance downgrade is a *supply* decision management can reverse quickly (*"as the time came back in a conducive form, I think we should be able to pick up quickly"*). Login-to-sanction is therefore the single leading indicator to track: 45%-47% now vs a 55%-58% normal. That makes this a **throttle, not a brake** — a distinction most affordable-HFC slowdowns don't offer.
- **The AUM guidance is load-bearing on BT-out, which is cyclically flattered.** Management admits low BT-out is partly an artefact of a cautious market (*"you always find for everyone BT-out is always normally on a lower side"*). Growth guided at 27%-28% AUM off 20% disbursements only works while runoff stays suppressed — so an *improving* macro would paradoxically pressure the AUM bridge even as it lifts disbursements.
- **DA and co-lending are PBC instruments, not strategy.** Both exist to shift LAP off-book and hold PBC at 64% vs the 60% floor. Read the "softness in DA drawdown" and the co-lending stall as regulatory-ratio management, not a change in business model — and note the company is content to abandon co-lending entirely (*"it is not something which we have to worry around at all"*), unusual among peers building it as a growth channel.
- **Rate-cycle asymmetry is now deliberately engineered.** Only ~7%-8% of the fixed-rate book is funded by variable-rate liabilities (from ~33% two years ago, heading to ~5%). India Shelter has been converting a falling-rate windfall into structural rate-risk removal rather than into growth — consistent with the "return ratios rather than growth alone" framing in the opening remarks.
- **The 9.5% margin should not be extrapolated.** Q4 NPA-resolution interest recovery is in it, and disbursement yield already prints below portfolio yield. The >6% *spread* commitment, not the margin level, is the number management has actually bound itself to.
- **Silent on the reduction in ROE headroom from over-provisioning:** ECL at 2x the regulatory requirement plus a 2% Stage-2 overlay is a conservative posture that management says it will *not* extend further — meaning FY27 credit cost of 40-50 bps has no further buffer-build inside it, which is mildly favourable for FY27 PAT.

one-line thesis: A clean FY26 finish — AUM Rs. 11,044 crores (+29% YoY), first-ever Rs. 1,000 crore+ disbursement quarter, PAT Rs. 138 crores (+27% YoY), ROE 17.6%, and Gross Stage-3 down to 1.2% as SARFAESI resolutions from the Q2 NPA bulge came through organically. The real news is a **deliberate step-down in the growth ambition**: medium-term guidance cut from the earlier 30%-35% to **25%-30% loan growth**, with FY27 disbursement growth guided only "beyond 20%", because management has purposely tightened the business rule engine — login-to-sanction has fallen from a normal 55%-58% to 45%-47% (having bottomed at 40%-43%). Management frames this as temporary caution in a "cautionary environment" (Middle East war, LPG shortage, uneven monsoon), not a demand problem, and holds the Rs. 30,000 crore-by-2030 AUM goal on 27%-28% CAGR. Spread discipline (>6%) and a 2x-regulatory ECL buffer are the trade-off for the slower top line.

But our business rule engine, the credit engine that has to function that isn't titled up purposely keeping mind all the aspects which is happening there. So, we have been a little cautious in that way."* Distribution base: **307 branches, 15 states, 4,800 employees**; digital channel now disbursing **Rs. 20-30 crores** (vs "single digit" a year to eighteen months ago).

Standalone HFC, no subsidiaries discussed.

- **Productivity drive** — "per case, per employee, number of cases that has to keep improving" in the *same* geographies.
- **Digital origination:** from single-digit crores to **Rs. 20-30 crores** of disbursement, started ~a year ago.
- **Ticket-size creep:** growth in the 15-25 lakh and 25 lakh+ buckets is real but off "almost negligible base" and only "handful of cases"; ATS ~Rs. 10 lakh, guided to *"maybe 10.5 in, say, 2, 3, 4 quarters beyond"* — explicitly **not** an immediate lever.
- **Balance-sheet headroom:** leverage 3x against an analyst-cited ~55% capital adequacy, unused until 4.5x.
6a. moat & competitive position:
- **Diversification-as-underwriting-moat, evidenced by scale:** *"our distribution is spread across 15 states. At this scale, at this level, very few companies have experimented to go into those markets at all. With time, the maturity is coming, that prudency is coming in terms of underwriting, as we keep creating our own vintage in these kind of states."*
- **Collateral quality:** **~98% of the LAP book is SORP** — an unusually hard collateral base for a LAP-heavy affordable lender, and the reason SARFAESI resolution works organically.
- **Retention machine lowering BT-out:** BT-out down to **4.5%, −80 bps YoY, "lowest among last 3-4 years"**, attributed to a customer-engagement unit set up ~a year ago plus a customer app *"which have now almost all the customers which is on our board"*. Management is candid that part of this is cyclical, not structural: *"In particular time when situation is always alarming and cautionary… you always find for everyone BT-out is always normally on a lower side basically."*
- **Fixed-rate book as a BT-out shield:** ~48% of AUM is pure fixed-rate, +37% semi-variable (fixed for the first three years) — CFO: *"that is again one of the good sectors which support us in terms of BT-out."*
- **Barrier framing on competition:** *"any new player which is entering, they have their own hurdles around that piece to venture that market… It is only your ability to execute in those markets that matters."*
margins & cost dynamics:
Yield held with a **10 bps YoY decline in portfolio yield to 14.8%** while Q4 disbursement yield printed **14.6%** — i.e. new business is being written a touch below the back book. On the liability side, **bucket cost of funds 8.2%** and **Q4 marginal cost of funds 7.9%**, so incremental spreads are the wider ones; management explicitly credits the rate cycle: *"this has been a great year in terms of your cost of borrowing, because of market slashing down in terms of cost, and we get a benefit on that piece."* Cost of borrowing was down "about 10 to 15 basis points" in the quarter — which the analyst correctly noted does **not** explain the full 9.1% → 9.5% margin move; the CFO closed the gap with the **NPA-resolution interest recovery** (see §2 one-offs).

**Funding structure:** >30 counterparties, **NHB share stable at 15%**, **average borrowing tenure >8 years**. Q4 saw a **Rs. 378 crore NHB drawdown at 7.5%** with *"a balance of more than Rs. 300 crores for drawdown in Q1."*

**Asset-liability rate mix (CFO's reiterated, authoritative version at the end of the call):** ~**15%** of AUM variable-rate · ~**37%** semi-variable (fixed for three years then variable) · ~**48%** pure fixed. Of that 48% fixed book: ~25% funded by equity, ~17% by fixed-rate borrowings, and the residual **7%-8%** is fixed-rate assets funded by variable-rate liabilities — down from ~33% in Mar-24, targeted to ~5% in FY27. ⚠️ Earlier in the same Q&A the CFO gave a materially different cut (*"around 13%-14% of book which is on floating… that book is again now around 10%-12%, which means approximately 70%, 65%-70% book that continue to remain on the fixed"*), which prompted Kunal Shah's clarification request. Both are recorded; the 15/37/48 reiteration is the one management chose to restate.

**Cost line:** OPEX +26% YoY against AUM +29% → OPEX/AUM **3.94%**, −20 bps, and cost-to-income **36%**, ~−100 bps, for both quarter and year.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): Physical capex is branch roll-out only. **41 branches added in FY26** (6 in Q4) to reach **307**, against a standing **40-45 per year** cadence and a **500-branch by 2030** ambition. No commissioning dates or lumpy capex. The slippage risk here is not construction but the **branch-vintage-to-productivity lag**, which management asserts is improving mechanically as the denominator grows.
capital allocation: Net worth **Rs. 3,198 crores**; leverage **3x**; capital adequacy ~55% (analyst-stated, uncontested). Explicit sequencing: grow into the balance sheet to **4x-4.5x leverage** first, and only then consider *"whether to raise the funds, QIP or something"*. No dividend or buyback commentary on this call. Off-book channels (DA at 15%-16%, co-lending ~4%-5%) are used to manage the **PBC ratio at 64% vs a 60% regulatory threshold**, not to release capital. Provisioning policy is deliberately over-capitalised relative to rules: **Rs. 87 crores ECL vs Rs. 47 crores** required — *"we have created a briefly 2x buffer of what the regulatory threshold. And we have always kept that kind of threshold historically."*
risks & watch-items:
- **The growth guidance was cut, and the cut is management-chosen.** 30%-35% → 25%-30%; login-to-sanction throttled to 45%-47% via the BRE. If the "cautionary environment" persists, FY27 disbursement growth of "beyond 20%" is the floor that has to hold for the 27%-28% AUM CAGR to work.
- **The AUM-vs-disbursement growth gap is unresolved.** Two analysts (Mayank Mistry, Satyam Kumar) pressed on how ~20% disbursement growth produces ~27% AUM growth; the answer was **only** falling BT-out — *"anything above 20% on that piece is going to stretch to the positivity"* — with no quantified runoff bridge. If BT-out stops falling (and management concedes the current low is partly a cautious-cycle artefact), the AUM guidance breaks.
- **Margin quality:** the 9.5% print embeds non-recurring Q4 NPA-resolution interest; disbursement yield (14.6%) is already below portfolio yield (14.8%).
- **Macro on the borrower base:** Middle East war → **LPG / commercial gas supply disruption**, uneven and abnormal monsoon hitting agricultural cash flows and informal income. MD: *"instantly we don't feel that there is any impact in terms of their behavior particularly, but still we feel it's a watchful situation… Things look okay till the month of March."* **The call explicitly defers the read to the following quarter** — *"This quarter is going to play, give output in terms of that piece."*
- **Asset-quality improvement is mechanical, not fresh-flow.** GS3 1.2% came from SARFAESI resolution of the Q2 bulge on a 6-8 month lag; the Stage-2 overlay suggests management itself is not calling an all-clear.
- **Regulatory:** RBI's ECL circular sets minimum 1.5% (home loan) / 2.5% (LAP) thresholds — CFO says *"they are not applicable to us"*, but the company pre-emptively buffered to Stage-2 anyway. **CLM-1 co-lending remains blocked with no timeline.**
- **Two internally inconsistent disclosures on this one call** — co-lending 4% (MD) vs 5% (CFO) of book, and two different fixed/floating asset splits. Minor individually, but both concern the same LAP/rate-risk area.
- **Concentration:** Rajasthan still 30%+ of AUM; the de-concentration path is a five-year one.
management quality / tone:
Confident and specific on operating metrics (login ratios, branch math, rate-reset buckets) and notably willing to disclose a **self-imposed slowdown** rather than dress it as demand weakness — the BRE-tightening admission and the login-ratio disclosure are the kind of numbers most lenders bury. The CFO volunteered the NPA-resolution distortion in the NIM **without being asked**, which is a genuine credibility marker. Tone is candid on macro uncertainty (*"we have to keep our fingers crossed"*; *"instantly today we don't have answer for that piece"*) rather than promotional.

Against that: the guidance downgrade from 30%-35% to 25%-30% was **not surfaced in the opening remarks** — it took Kunal Shah's question to name it as a change. The MD deflected a direct question on whether Q4 was the disbursement-growth bottom (*"Please don't allow me to compare between Q4 and how the Q1 has to work on"*), and the competition answer was pure assertion (*"it is not a point of concern at all"*) with no data. English is loose throughout ("plundered by all kinds of competition", "that isn't titled up purposely"), so several answers require careful reading. Two numeric self-contradictions in one call (§10) is a small but real disclosure-discipline flag.
non-obvious takeaways:
- **The binding constraint is the credit engine, not demand.** Logins are rising while sanctions are being cut — the guidance downgrade is a *supply* decision management can reverse quickly (*"as the time came back in a conducive form, I think we should be able to pick up quickly"*). Login-to-sanction is therefore the single leading indicator to track: 45%-47% now vs a 55%-58% normal. That makes this a **throttle, not a brake** — a distinction most affordable-HFC slowdowns don't offer.
- **The AUM guidance is load-bearing on BT-out, which is cyclically flattered.** Management admits low BT-out is partly an artefact of a cautious market (*"you always find for everyone BT-out is always normally on a lower side"*). Growth guided at 27%-28% AUM off 20% disbursements only works while runoff stays suppressed — so an *improving* macro would paradoxically pressure the AUM bridge even as it lifts disbursements.
- **DA and co-lending are PBC instruments, not strategy.** Both exist to shift LAP off-book and hold PBC at 64% vs the 60% floor. Read the "softness in DA drawdown" and the co-lending stall as regulatory-ratio management, not a change in business model — and note the company is content to abandon co-lending entirely (*"it is not something which we have to worry around at all"*), unusual among peers building it as a growth channel.
- **Rate-cycle asymmetry is now deliberately engineered.** Only ~7%-8% of the fixed-rate book is funded by variable-rate liabilities (from ~33% two years ago, heading to ~5%). India Shelter has been converting a falling-rate windfall into structural rate-risk removal rather than into growth — consistent with the "return ratios rather than growth alone" framing in the opening remarks.
- **The 9.5% margin should not be extrapolated.** Q4 NPA-resolution interest recovery is in it, and disbursement yield already prints below portfolio yield. The >6% *spread* commitment, not the margin level, is the number management has actually bound itself to.
- **Silent on the reduction in ROE headroom from over-provisioning:** ECL at 2x the regulatory requirement plus a 2% Stage-2 overlay is a conservative posture that management says it will *not* extend further — meaning FY27 credit cost of 40-50 bps has no further buffer-build inside it, which is mildly favourable for FY27 PAT.

hero.oneLiner: A clean FY26 finish — AUM Rs. 11,044 crores (+29% YoY), first-ever Rs. 1,000 crore+ disbursement quarter, PAT Rs. 138 crores (+27% YoY), ROE 17.6%, and Gross Stage-3 down to 1.2% as SARFAESI resolutions from the Q2 NPA bulge came through organically. The real news is a **deliberate step-down in the growth ambition**: medium-term guidance cut from the earlier 30%-35% to **25%-30% loan growth**, with FY27 disbursement growth guided only "beyond 20%", because management has purposely tightened the business rule engine — login-to-sanction has fallen from a normal 55%-58% to 45%-47% (having bottomed at 40%-43%). Management frames this as temporary caution in a "cautionary environment" (Middle East war, LPG shortage, uneven monsoon), not a demand problem, and holds the Rs. 30,000 crore-by-2030 AUM goal on 27%-28% CAGR. Spread discipline (>6%) and a 2x-regulatory ECL buffer are the trade-off for the slower top line.
